title: प्रथमोनुवाकः
samhita: यामिषु॑-ङ्गिरिशन्त॒ हस्ते॒ बिभ॒र्​ष्यस्त॑वे । शि॒वा-ङ्गि॑रित्र॒ ता-ङ्कु॑रु॒ मा हिग्ं॑सीः॒ पुरु॑ष॒-ञ्जग॑त् ॥
pada:
याम । इषु᳚म । गि॒रि॒-श॒न्तेति॑ गिरि = श॒न्त॒। हस्ते᳚ । बिभ॑र्षि । अस्त॑वे  ॥ 
शि॒वाम । गि॒रि॒त्रेति॑ गिरि = त्र॒ । ताम । कु॒रु॒ । मा । हि॒ग्ं॒सीः॒ । पुरु॑षम । जग॑त ॥
krama: यामिषु॑म् । इषु॑-ङ्गिरिशन्त । गि॒रि॒शन्त॒ हस्ते॑ । हस्ते॒ बिभ॑र्षि । बिभ॒र्​ष्यस्त॑वे । अस्त॑वे॒ति अस्त॑वे । शि॒वा-ङ्गि॑रित्र । गि॒रि॒त्र॒ ताम् । ता-ङ्कु॑रु । कु॒रु॒ मा । मा हि॑ग्ं-सीः । हि॒ग्ं॒सीः पुरु॑षम् । पुरु॑ष॒-ञ्जग॑त् । जग॒दिति॑ जग॑त् ॥

sayana.text: O Girishanta, that arrow (ishu) which you hold in your hand to throw (astave) at enemies. "Giritra" means he who protects or guards (trayate) the mountain (giri) named Kailasa. O Rudra, make that arrow held in your hand auspicious (shiva), peaceful towards us. Do not harm our human people (purusham) or our 'jagat'—moving beings other than humans, like cattle etc. (4)

bhatta_bhaskara.dhyana: Meditation on Shiva as detailed in standard commentaries.
bhatta_bhaskara.text:
For the two mantras 'Yamishum girishanta' and 'Shivenavachasa', the Rishi is Gautama. Some say Godhuma. The Deity is Rudra. 'Yamishum' is in Nichrit-Anushtup metre. 'Shivenavachasa' is in Anushtup. By these two, the fierce body engaged in the burning of Tripura is pacified. O Girishanta—explained already. That arrow which you hold (bibharshi) in your hand. For what purpose? To throw (astave) at the demons who are to be killed, after the request of the gods. As the gods said: "Who will throw this (arrow)?... Rudra is indeed cruel, let him throw it." He said "Let a boon (be given) to me." Or, after the burning of the straw of Tripura, that arrow which you hold in your hand to withdraw, having fulfilled its purpose as instructed—make that arrow auspicious (shiva), welfare-causing. Just as it targets only those to be killed, it should be understood as protecting your devotees. 'Ma himsiih'—do not harm me...
...



...a person (purusha) of righteous conduct. Indeed, he alone deserves the designation of 'Purusha'. Furthermore, 'jagat'—the moving world like cattle, buffaloes, etc., which are other than humans—do not harm those either, by implication. Do not harm even the stationary things like trees and creepers. Thus, by excluding humans etc. and making the arrow target only those to be killed [the wicked], that constitutes the arrow's auspiciousness (shivatva). O Giritra—he who protects (trayate) the mountain (giri) Kailasa, holding it in high regard as his residence. Or, the protector of the cloud (giri) because he causes it to rain. Or, the protector of the chariot which is like a mountain, by being the protector of the gods who are its parts. Or, the protector (palaka) of words (giraam), i.e., words of prayer, by granting boons as desired.

abhinava_shankara.dhyana: Meditation on Lord Maheshvara with resplendent Goddess.
abhinava_shankara.text:
Whatever arrow, O Girishanta (He who confers welfare on those
        dwelling in the mountain), You hold in Your hand for shooting —
        make it auspicious, O Giritra (Protector of the pledge); do not
        harm our men or our cattle.

Having thus prayed in the second and third [mantras] for the attainment of
the desired [objectives], in the fourth mantra the removal of the undesired
is prayed for: "yam ishum" — O Girishanta (He who abides on the mountain
and extends welfare to the people), whatever arrow You hold in Your hand —
for what purpose? To shoot (astave) and strike down the wicked sinners; the
suffix "tave" is in the dative sense of "in order to shoot."

Make that arrow shiva (auspicious) — O You who are shiva-kara (the maker
of auspiciousness), the intent [of the address] is: You who can make the
arrow auspicious, [please do so]. In what does the auspiciousness of the
arrow consist? That is answered: "ma himsih" — do not harm our men
(purusha) — our sons, grandsons, and others; and [do not harm] our cattle,
buffaloes, homes, gardens, fields, and all the rest that is ours. This
constitutes the making of the arrow auspicious. Such is the intent.

Now, since the [first] address "girishanta" has already served its purpose,
the additional address "giritra" conveys a distinct meaning — let us show
what that is: The promise of the Supreme Lord is: "Even if one has done
something improper, if he takes refuge in me, I shall protect him." Hence it
is heard in the Nabhanedishtha anuvaka (section): having first narrated the
story of Manu's son [Nabhanedishtha] — "Manu Nabhanedishtha yajnavasau
rudra bhagacha so 'danat 'mama va ime pashava' iti udurve 'mahyam
imani' ity atvabibhat vai tasya ta ishata ity atrabhavit 'yad yajnavasau
hiyate mama vai tad' idi tatsadyagravara-tunabhyavetyamu" — having recounted
this story of Nabhanedishtha, and then, addressing him, [Shiva's] promise
is heard: "yajne ma bhajatha te pashvabha abhiyamsye" (worship Me in
the sacrifice and I shall give you cattle). So too in the Puranas and in
esoteric texts, many statements of this kind are found on this subject.

Accordingly, "Giritra" means: He who, abiding in the speech (giri) that
has the form of a vow (pratijnya), protects (trayate) those who worship
Him — O Giritra! [The intent of this address is:] even for one who has
acted improperly [but has become Your devotee] — in the manner of
Nabhanedishtha — protect their sons and grandsons who worship You.

Thus [ends] the fourth mantra.
